st: Put the ground lamb, ground beef, grated onion, minced garlic, [[1 tbsp]] paprika, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper in a large bowl.
Knead the mixture with your hands for about 5 minutes until it turns sticky and paste-like. This helps it hold together when sliced.
Press the meat firmly into a loaf pan lined with plastic wrap, packing out all air pockets. Cover and chill for [[2 hours]] so it firms up.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Turn the loaf out onto a rack set over a baking tray and brush it with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes, until browned and the center reads 160°F (71°C). Rest the loaf for 10 minutes.
Slice the meat as thinly as you can with a sharp knife. Fry the slices in a hot dry skillet for 2 minutes to crisp the edges.
Stir [[1 clove]] grated garlic into the yogurt with a pinch of salt to make the sauce.
Warm the flatbreads, fill with the meat, sliced tomatoes and red onion, and spoon the garlic yogurt over the top.
Put the lamb, soft lamb fat or butter, grated onion, garlic, chili flakes, chopped bell pepper and salt in a bowl.
Knead the mix by hand for about 6 minutes until it is very smooth and sticky. Cover and chill for [[1 hour]].
Soak four flat metal skewers if you have them. Wet your hands and press a quarter of the meat around each skewer into a long flat shape, about 1 inch wide.
Rub the whole bell peppers with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil. Heat a grill or cast iron grill pan over high heat.
Grill the peppers, turning, until blistered, about 10 minutes. Move them aside.
Grill the kebabs for 3 to 4 minutes per side until browned outside and cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Toss the sliced red onion with [[1 tbsp]] sumac and the parsley.
Slide the meat off the skewers onto warm flatbread. Serve with the grilled peppers and sumac onions.

ing: sliced very thin, or ground beef shaped as doner
st: Mix the beef with [[2 cloves]] minced garlic, [[1 tsp]] salt, the pepper and [[1 tbsp]] olive oil. Marinate for [[1 hour]] in the fridge.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] olive oil in a large skillet over high heat. Cook the beef in two batches for 3 to 4 minutes each until browned and cooked through (160°F or 71°C for ground beef).
In a small pot, simmer the tomato sauce, tomato paste, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and paprika for 8 minutes.
Mix the yogurt with [[1 clove]] minced garlic and a pinch of salt.
Toast the pita pieces in a dry pan or the oven until crisp at the edges, and lay them on a platter.
Spoon the hot tomato sauce over the bread, then pile the cooked beef on top.
Melt the butter in a small pan until foamy and lightly golden. Pour it sizzling over the meat.
Serve right away with the garlic yogurt on the side.
Mix the flour, yeast and [[1 tsp]] salt. Stir in the warm water and olive oil, then knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover the dough and let it rise for [[1 hour]] until doubled.
Mix the beef, onion, tomatoes, bell pepper, tomato paste, parsley, paprika and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a bowl. Make it a loose, spreadable paste.
Heat the oven to 500°F (260°C) with a baking sheet inside.
Divide the dough into 6 balls. Roll each into a very thin round about 8 inches wide.
Spread a thin layer of meat topping over each round, going almost to the edge.
Bake each lahmacun on the hot sheet for 5 to 6 minutes until the edges are crisp and the meat is cooked.
Squeeze lemon over the top, add some parsley, and roll up to eat.
Mix the flour, yeast and [[2 tsp]] salt, then add the warm water and olive oil. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise for [[1 hour]] until doubled.
Cook the beef and onion in a skillet over medium-high heat for about 8 minutes until the beef is no longer pink. Add the tomato and paprika and cook 3 more minutes. Let it cool.
Heat the oven to 475°F (245°C) with a baking sheet inside.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces. Roll each into an oval about 10 inches long.
Spread meat and cheese along the center, leaving a border. Fold the long edges inward and pinch the ends into a boat shape.
Beat 1 egg and brush the edges. Bake on the hot sheet for 12 to 15 minutes until golden.
Crack an egg into the center of each pide, bake 2 to 3 more minutes until the white sets, and serve.
Mix the flour, egg, [[1 tsp]] salt and the warm water into a stiff dough. Knead for 8 minutes, then cover and rest for [[30 minutes]].
Mix the beef, onion, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper for the filling.
Roll the dough very thin on a floured counter and cut it into 1-inch squares.
Put a tiny bit of filling, about the size of a chickpea, in the center of each square. Pinch the corners together to close.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Spread the manti on an oiled baking tray and bake for 15 minutes until lightly browned.
Bring a big pot of salted water to a boil. Add the baked manti and boil for 5 minutes, then drain, keeping a little broth.
Stir the garlic into the yogurt with a pinch of salt.
Melt the butter in a small pan, stir in the paprika and mint for 30 seconds. Spoon the yogurt over the manti and drizzle the butter on top.
Heat the olive oil and butter in a wide skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and salt. Cook for about 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the juices cook down.
Lightly beat the eggs in a small bowl.
Pour the eggs over the tomato mixture. Lower the heat and stir gently for about 2 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat while the eggs are still soft and slightly wet, since they keep cooking.
Sprinkle with the pepper flakes and serve right in the pan with bread for dipping.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrots for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, potato, water and salt. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat.
Simmer for 25 minutes, until the lentils and vegetables are very soft.
Blend the soup with an immersion blender until smooth, adding a splash of water if too thick.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in a small pan, stir in the paprika for 20 seconds, and swirl it over the soup.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.
Peel strips of skin from the eggplants lengthwise to make stripes. Soak them in salted water for [[30 minutes]], then pat dry.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] olive oil in a skillet and fry the eggplants, turning, for 8 minutes until lightly browned. Set aside.
In the same pan, cook the onions in [[2 tbsp]] oil for 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes, parsley, sugar, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Cook for 5 minutes, then take off the heat.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Cut a long slit in each eggplant and gently open it into a pocket.
Sprinkle the pockets with [[1 tsp]] salt and stuff them with the filling. Arrange them snugly in a baking dish.
Pour the water, remaining oil and lemon juice around the eggplants. Cover with foil.
Bake for 40 minutes until very tender. Let cool and serve warm or at room temperature.
Put the beef, onion, garlic, breadcrumbs, egg, cumin, paprika, parsley, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Knead by hand for 3 minutes until the mixture feels sticky and holds together.
Cover and chill for [[30 minutes]] so the flavors settle and the meat firms up.
Shape into oval patties or sausage shapes, about 2 inches long.
Heat a grill or skillet over medium-high heat and brush with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Cook the kofte for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until browned and the center reaches 160°F (71°C).
Rest for 3 minutes and serve with salad, rice or bread.
Make the syrup first. Boil the sugar and water for 10 minutes, stir in the lemon juice, then let it cool completely.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Brush a 9x13-inch pan with melted butter.
Mix the walnuts, pistachios and cinnamon in a bowl.
Lay 8 phyllo sheets in the pan, brushing each with butter. Keep the remaining sheets covered with a damp towel.
Sprinkle half the nut mixture on top, then layer 4 more buttered sheets, the rest of the nuts, and 8 buttered sheets on top.
Cut the baklava into diamonds with a sharp knife before baking, cutting all the way through.
Pour the remaining butter over the top. Bake for 50 minutes until deep golden.
Pour the cooled syrup over the hot baklava, then cool for at least [[4 hours]] before serving.
Mix the flour, yeast, salt and sugar. Add the warm water and knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Oil a bowl, add the dough, cover, and let rise for [[1 hour]].
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment.
Whisk the molasses with the dipping water in a wide dish. Spread the sesame seeds in another.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces. Roll each into a 20-inch rope, fold in half and twist, then join the ends into a ring.
Dip each ring in the molasses mixture, then press into the sesame seeds to coat well.
Place on the trays and bake for 15 to 18 minutes until deep golden.
Cool on a rack. Best eaten the same day.
Place the eggs in a pot of cold water, bring to a boil, then cook for 10 minutes so the yolks are fully set and safe. Cool in cold water and peel.
Set the beyaz peynir and kaşar out 20 minutes before serving. Cut the beyaz peynir into thick slabs and fan the kaşar slices.
Slice the tomatoes and cucumbers into rounds and shingle them on a plate with a pinch of salt. Cut the eggs in half.
Pan-fry the sucuk slices in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes per side until the edges crisp, then move them to a plate.
Put the olives in two small bowls. Spoon [[3 tbsp]] honey and [[3 tbsp]] jam into two more, and the kaymak into a fourth bowl.
Slice the simit or bread and set it in a basket. Place everything in the center of the table in small plates so guests can graze. Serve with hot tea.
nt: Eggs boiled and sucuk pan-fried; everything else: don't cook, just sliced and arranged
Best swap: feta for beyaz peynir and mozzarella for kaşar; skip the sucuk and add extra eggs or menemen-style tomato for a vegetarian spread.

st: Simmer the rinsed rice with [[1 cup]] water in a medium pot over medium-low heat for 10 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Add the milk and bring to a gentle boil. Lower the heat and simmer 25 minutes, stirring often so the bottom does not scorch.
Stir in [[0.75 cup]] sugar. Mix the cornstarch with [[0.25 cup]] cold milk, pour it in, and stir 3 minutes until the pudding coats a spoon. Add the vanilla.
Heat the oven broiler to high. Ladle the pudding into 6 oven safe bowls and let them cool for 10 minutes.
Brush each surface lightly with beaten egg yolk. Broil on the top rack 2 to 3 minutes, watching closely, until the tops are spotted dark brown.
Cool to room temperature, then chill at least 2 hours. Dust with cinnamon before serving.
nt: Simmered on the stove, then broiled until browned
Best swap: a kitchen torch instead of the broiler to char the top, and oat milk for dairy-free, same amounts.

st: Measure the cold water into the cezve using a demitasse cup as your guide. Cold water gives the slowest, foamiest brew.
Add [[2 tbsp]] of coffee and [[2 tsp]] sugar if you like it sweet. Stir once gently until just mixed, then do not stir again.
Set the cezve over the lowest heat. Heat slowly for 3 to 4 minutes; the coffee will sink and a dark foam will start forming at the edges.
Watch closely as the foam darkens and slowly rises toward the rim. Just before it boils over, pull the cezve off the heat.
Spoon a little foam into each cup, then return the pot to the heat for a few seconds to rise once more. Pour the rest gently so the foam stays on top.
Let the grounds settle for 1 minute and sip slowly. Do not drink the thick sludge at the bottom.
nt: Slowly brewed in a cezve over very low heat, never boiled hard
Best swap: no cezve, use a tiny saucepan; no powder-fine grind, grind espresso as finely as your grinder allows.

st: Line an 8 inch square pan with oiled parchment. Combine the sugar, [[1.5 cups]] water and lemon juice in a pot and stir over medium heat until dissolved.
Boil the syrup without stirring until a candy thermometer reads 240°F, about 12 minutes. Take the pot off the heat.
In a second large pot, whisk the cornstarch, cream of tartar and remaining [[2 cups]] water until smooth, then heat over medium, whisking, until thick and glue-like.
Slowly whisk the hot syrup into the starch paste. Simmer on low, whisking often, until golden and very thick, about 60 minutes. Watch for spitting.
Stir in the rosewater and pistachios, then scrape into the pan and smooth the top.
Let set uncovered at room temperature for 8 hours. Cut into cubes with an oiled knife and toss in powdered sugar.
nt: Simmered to 240°F, then set
Best swap: use [[0.5 cup]] cornstarch plus a pinch of salt if cornflour is not on hand, and orange blossom water instead of rosewater.

ing: about 1 lb each, gutted and scaled
st: Rinse the fish and pat dry inside and out. Slash the skin diagonally 3 times on each side down to the bone so it cooks evenly.
Rub with [[1 tbsp]] oil and [[1 tsp]] salt. Tuck lemon slices, thyme and garlic into the cavity.
Heat a grill to medium-high, about 450°F. Clean the grate and oil it well with a folded towel dipped in oil so the skin does not stick.
Grill the fish 6 to 7 minutes on the first side without moving it until the skin releases easily and has dark grill marks.
Flip gently with a wide spatula and grill 5 to 6 minutes more. It is done when the flesh at the bone reads 140°F and flakes.
Transfer to a plate, drizzle with [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and lemon juice, and serve with arugula and wedges.
nt: Grilled whole over medium-high direct heat
Best swap: roast on an oiled tray at 450°F for 18 to 20 minutes. Branzino or red snapper replace sea bream one for one.

ing: only if juice is too strong
st: Roll each pomegranate on the counter, pressing firmly, to loosen the seeds inside.
Cut off the crown, score the skin in sections, and break the fruit apart in a bowl of water. The seeds sink and the white pith floats; skim off the pith.
Drain the seeds and blend them for 10 seconds, only until they burst. Do not pulverize, which makes the juice bitter.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the pulp, and taste. Add [[1 tsp]] sugar only if the fruit is very tart.
Serve right away over ice, or chill up to 2 days.
nt: Don't cook: deseed, pulse and strain
Best swap: no fresh fruit, use 3 cups unsweetened bottled pomegranate juice; a citrus juicer can squeeze halved fruit directly.

st: Heat a grill or the oven broiler to high. Prick the eggplants with a fork and cook them 25 minutes, turning until the skin is blackened and the flesh collapses.

Rest the eggplants in a covered bowl 10 minutes, then peel and drain the flesh in a sieve. Chop it fine and mix with [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice, [[1 clove]] garlic, [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and salt. Add [[0.5 cup]] yogurt to make patlican salatasi.
For haydari, stir [[1.5 cup]] yogurt, [[1 clove]] garlic, the dill, the feta and a pinch of salt together until thick and speckled. Chill.
For acili ezme, mix the tomatoes, red onion, chili, parsley, pomegranate molasses, pul biber, [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and salt. Let it sit 10 minutes so juices gather.
Spoon each meze into its own small bowl. Drizzle a little olive oil over the haydari and eggplant.
Serve cold, with warm sliced bread and something to drink alongside.
nt: Eggplant charred over open flame or under the broiler; haydari and ezme: don't cook
Best swap: for haydari, plain Greek yogurt works as is; use 1 cup of drained vegan yogurt for dairy-free.

st: Mix the feta, parsley, egg yolk and pepper into a chunky filling. Whisk the flour and water into a thin paste for sealing.
Stack the phyllo and cut each sheet into 3 long triangles. Keep them under a damp towel so they do not dry out.
Place [[1 tbsp]] filling at the wide end of a triangle, fold in the sides and roll up tightly like a cigar. Seal the tip with the paste.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 340°F, about 1 inch deep.
Fry the rolls in batches 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden. Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
nt: Deep fried (or baked at 400°F)
Best swap: bake the rolls 20 minutes at 400°F brushed with oil, or use ricotta mixed with a pinch of salt for feta.

st: Stir the yogurt with the garlic and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Spread it into two shallow bowls.
Bring a wide pan of water to a gentle simmer and add [[1 tbsp]] vinegar. Crack each egg into a cup first.
Swirl the water and slide in the eggs one at a time. Poach for 3 minutes until the whites are firm and yolks soft. Cook eggs fully if serving to anyone vulnerable.
Lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon, blot on a towel and set two on each bed of yogurt.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a small pan until foaming. Stir in the Aleppo pepper for 20 seconds off the heat so it does not burn.
Pour the red butter over the eggs, sprinkle with the mint and serve at once with bread.
nt: Poached, no frying for the eggs
Best swap: use paprika with a pinch of cayenne for Aleppo pepper, 1 tsp paprika plus 0.25 tsp cayenne.

st: Dice the tomatoes, cucumbers and green peppers into pieces about 1/2 inch wide and place them in a big bowl.
Slice or cut the parsley leaves finely, discarding thick stems, so every bite has a little green.
Finely dice the onion, rinse it in cold water for 30 seconds to remove sharpness and add to the bowl with the parsley.
Whisk [[3 tbsp]] lemon juice, [[3 tbsp]] olive oil, [[1 tsp]] sumac and salt together.
Pour the dressing over, toss gently and serve right away so the vegetables stay crisp.
Taste for salt and acidity, and serve with grilled meat, eggs or fresh bread.
nt: Don't cook: finely chopped and tossed
Best swap: pomegranate molasses, 1 tbsp in place of lemon juice and sumac, for a sweeter tang.

st: Spoon [[2 cup]] cold plain yogurt into a large pitcher or blender jar. Use full fat yogurt for a creamy body.
Add [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 cup]] of the cold water. Whisk hard or blend on low for 30 seconds until completely smooth with no lumps.
Pour in the remaining [[1 cup]] cold water and blend or whisk for 1 minute more until the top turns frothy.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if it tastes flat. It should be refreshing and lightly salty, never sweet.
Pour over ice into tall glasses, sprinkle a little dried mint if you like, and serve right away.
nt: Don't cook: just whisk or blend
Best swap: use kefir for the yogurt for a tangier, fizzier ayran, or thin Greek yogurt at 1 part yogurt to 1 part water.

st: In a small bowl, mix [[1.5 tbsp]] sahlep powder with [[3 tbsp]] sugar so the powder does not clump in the hot milk.
Pour [[3 cup]] milk into a saucepan and whisk in the sahlep and sugar mixture while the milk is still cold.
Heat over medium heat, whisking constantly, for 8 to 10 minutes until it bubbles gently at the edges and thickens to a pudding-like drink that coats the spoon.
Keep whisking for 1 more minute at a low simmer so the sahlep cooks through and loses its raw taste. Stir in the rose water if using.
Pour into mugs and dust generously with cinnamon. Drink hot while it is thick.
nt: Simmered on the stove, whisked constantly
Best swap: if you cannot find sahlep, whisk 2 tbsp cornstarch with 3 tbsp cold milk first, then add it in place of the powder.

st: Heat the oven to 425°F. Scrub the potatoes, prick them all over with a fork, rub with the olive oil and a good pinch of salt, and wrap each tightly in foil.
Bake directly on the oven rack until a knife slides into the center with no resistance, about 75 minutes.
Unwrap carefully, since steam escapes. Slice each potato open lengthwise, leaving the bottom skin intact, and squeeze the ends so the flesh pops up.
Scoop the flesh into a mash inside the skin with a fork. Mix in [[2 tbsp]] butter and half the cheese until the filling is creamy and stringy.
Pile on the rest of the cheese, then add the corn, pickles and olives in separate stripes.
Finish with the ketchup and mayonnaise and eat right away with a fork, straight from the potato.
nt: Baked at 425°F in foil, then mashed and loaded
Best swap: sharp cheddar or any good melting cheese works 1 to 1; a very hot air fryer at 400°F also bakes the potato in about 50 minutes.

st: Heat a small, wide skillet over medium heat. Add the sucuk rounds in a single layer, with no extra oil needed.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until the edges crisp and the red fat renders into the pan.
Add the butter and let it melt into the sausage fat.
Crack the eggs over the sucuk, keeping the yolks whole. Cover the pan and cook on medium-low until the whites are fully set, about 4 minutes. Cook until no runny whites remain.
Sprinkle with the Aleppo pepper and parsley. Bring the pan straight to the table and serve with bread for scooping and tomato slices.
nt: Pan-fried in sausage fat
Best swap: use beef pepperoni or chorizo if you cannot find sucuk, and drop the butter since those render less fat than the pan needs.

st: Warm the milk and sugar in a small pot until the sugar dissolves. Keep hot over low heat.
Melt the butter in a heavy pan over medium-low heat and add the pine nuts. Stir until golden, about 2 minutes.
Add the flour and stir constantly for 15 minutes until deep golden and smelling nutty.
Take the pan off the heat for 30 seconds, then pour in the hot milk. It will spit, so stand back.
Return to low heat and stir for 3 minutes until the halva is thick and pulls away from the sides.
Cover and rest for 10 minutes so it absorbs the liquid.
Shape into quenelles with two spoons and dust with cinnamon.
nt: Toasted on the stove
Best swap: use olive oil for the butter 1 to 1, and oat milk for the milk.

st: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 4 minutes until fragrant. Cool for 5 minutes.
Pulse the walnuts in a food processor into coarse crumbs, not butter.
Add the pepper paste, tomato paste, Aleppo pepper, garlic, cumin and salt and pulse to combine.
Add [[1 tbsp]] pomegranate molasses and pour in the olive oil while pulsing until a thick spreadable paste forms.
Taste and adjust the heat. Rest for 20 minutes so the flavors blend, then serve with bread or on eggs.
nt: Toasted nuts, then blended with no cooking
Best swap: roasted red bell pepper plus 1 tsp chili flakes if you cannot find biber salcasi.

st: Heat the oven to 325°F. Season the shanks well with salt and pepper.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and the butter in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the shanks 3 minutes per side until deeply browned. Set aside.
Add the onions and cook 6 minutes until soft. Stir in the tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Add the grated tomatoes, thyme, bay and [[2 cup]] hot water. Return the shanks, tuck in the garlic and cover tightly.
Braise in the oven for 2 hours, then add the carrots and potatoes and cook covered for 45 minutes, until the meat pulls from the bone.
Rest 10 minutes. Serve each shank with vegetables and the pan juices, with rice or bread.
nt: Seared, then braised in the oven
Best swap: use beef short ribs or bone-in lamb shoulder, with the same time.

st: Wash and prep the vegetables. Cut them into chunks and slit each pepper with a knife so brine can enter.
Boil [[5 cups]] water with [[0.33 cup]] salt for 3 minutes. Cool fully to room temperature, then stir in [[1 cup]] vinegar.
Layer vegetables, garlic, [[2 tbsp]] chickpeas and the beet slice in a clean large jar, packing them snugly.
Pour the cooled brine over, leaving 1 inch of space. Make sure everything is submerged.
Close the lid loosely and leave at room temperature for 5 to 7 days. The brine will turn cloudy and tangy.
Move to the refrigerator when sour enough. Serve cold with kebab, beans and rice. Keeps for several months.
nt: Brined cold, don't cook; ferments 5 to 7 days
Best swap: leave out the chickpeas and replace with a pinch of sugar; use lemon juice in place of vinegar for a milder tang.

st: Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and green pepper and cook 6 minutes until soft and translucent.
Stir in the tomato paste and red pepper paste and cook 2 minutes until it darkens and smells sweet.
Add the bulgur and stir 2 minutes to coat each grain in the oil.
Pour in the hot stock and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes.
Turn off the heat, lay a clean towel under the lid, and rest 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork and serve.
nt: Sauteed, then simmered covered and rested
Best swap: use fine bulgur and shorten simmer to 8 minutes, or sub 2 tsp tomato paste if you lack pepper paste.

ing: mackerel fillets, skin on, pin bones removed
crusty bread rolls or half baguettes
st: Pat the fillets dry, rub with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil, salt and pepper.
Heat a grill pan or cast iron skillet over high heat until smoking hot. Brush with the remaining oil.
Cook the fillets skin side down for 3 minutes without moving, flip and cook 2 minutes more. The flesh should flake and reach 145°F.
Toast the rolls on the pan for 1 minute so the cut sides crisp.
Toss the onion with [[1 tsp]] sumac, a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon.
Fill each roll with two fillets, lettuce, tomato and onion. Squeeze lemon over and serve right away.
nt: Grilled over high heat
Best swap: use sardines or sea bass fillets in place of mackerel. Bake the fish at 450°F for 8 minutes if you have no grill.

st: Rinse the cleaned anchovies and pat them dry. Salt lightly and let them sit for 10 minutes.
Mix the cornmeal and flour in a wide plate with a pinch of salt.
Press the anchovies into the cornmeal mix to coat both sides, shaking off the extra.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers, about 350°F.
Fry the anchovies in a single layer for 2 minutes per side until crisp and golden. Cook in batches.
Drain on paper towels and serve right away with lemon, arugula and red onion.
nt: Pan fried in cornmeal
Best swap: fresh sardines or smelts for the anchovies, same weight; use all cornmeal for gluten free.

st: Peel the eggplants in lengthwise stripes, leaving alternate strips of skin. Soak in salted water for 15 minutes, then pat dry.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the eggplants 8 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides and softening. Move to a baking dish.
In the same pan, cook the onion in [[1 tbsp]] oil for 5 minutes. Add the beef and cook 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, the chopped tomato, [[1 tsp]] salt and parsley. Cook 5 minutes until thick.
Heat the oven to 375°F. Slit each eggplant lengthwise down the middle without cutting through, and press the filling into the openings.
Top each with a tomato slice and half a green pepper. Pour [[0.5 cup]] hot water around them with the remaining oil.
Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 minutes until the eggplants are very tender.
nt: Fried, then baked at 375°F
Best swap: use cooked lentils or crumbled mushrooms in place of the beef at the same weight for a vegetarian filling.
